entries.topicDescription: Requesting and handling runtime permissions on Android.

tips.title: Runtime permissions flow
tips.content:
Since Android 6.0, dangerous permissions must be requested at runtime.
The flow: check → explain (optional) → request → handle result.

Always check if you already have the permission before requesting.
If the user denied before, show a rationale explaining WHY you need it.
If they denied twice, the system won't show the dialog again —
you need to direct them to Settings.

Common dangerous permissions: CAMERA, LOCATION, CONTACTS, MICROPHONE.

tips.title: Permissions in Compose with rememberLauncherForActivityResult
tips.content:
In Compose, use rememberLauncherForActivityResult to handle
permission requests declaratively.

Accompanist used to be the go-to library, but now the core
ActivityResultContracts work perfectly in Compose.

Keep the permission logic in the composable or ViewModel,
and show appropriate UI based on the permission state.

tips.title: Multiple permissions at once
tips.content:
Sometimes a feature needs multiple permissions
(e.g., video call needs CAMERA + RECORD_AUDIO).

Use RequestMultiplePermissions contract to ask for them together.
The result is a Map<String, Boolean> showing which were granted.

Handle partial grants gracefully — maybe the user allows the mic
but denies the camera. Offer degraded functionality where possible
instead of blocking the entire feature.
